newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada, China sign shipping agreement.
newsitem.headline: Canada, China sign shipping agreement.

text.p: Canada and China reached a bilateral maritime agreement on Friday aimed at facilitating ship traffic between the two countries.

The accord, Canada's first bilateral maritime pact, was due to be signed at a ceremony in Vancouver by Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson and Huang Zhendong, China's Minister of Communications.

"Today's agreement provides a foundation upon which our respective commercial maritime interests can expand their international activities. The new arrangement will also enhance Canada and China's longstanding commercial partnership," Anderson said.

The pact provides most-favored nation treatment for port access and the assessment of port charges, facilitates the opening of shipping-line ofices, gives companies relief from some Chinese tax and calls for closer cooperation in the investigation of marine accidents.
China traditionally enters into bilateral accords with major trading partners to maintain and expand its shipping operations, the Canadian government said.

The Chinese Overseas Shipping Company, overseen by China's communications ministry, ranks among the world's top five container lines and is one of the Port of Vancouver's biggest customers. Canada hopes the agreement will help increase the Chinese company's business in Vancouver by up to 50 percent.
